addressGoes: the repository's Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook, with content type application/json and GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET from your env file as its Secret, or the GitHub App's Webhook URL and secret

settings.description: The bot's GitHub username, as people @mention it: the account the token is for, or the GitHub App's name with [bot].
The secret GitHub signs each request with: any text of your own, entered as the webhook's Secret.

notes: **Each reply is a comment of its own** on the issue or pull request.

why.maxTextLength: GitHub refuses a comment longer than 65,536 characters (422, "Body is too long"), and the adapter sends a reply whole whatever its length. 65,000 is within it.
why.addressGoes: The adapter never gives GitHub the address. With a personal access token it is a webhook on the repository or organization, with the secret and the events Issue comments and Pull request review comments; a GitHub App has one Webhook URL in its own settings. The default content type, form-encoded, is one the adapter can't read.
why.settings: The adapter answers only a comment that mentions its userName, which is GITHUB_BOT_USERNAME or else the made-up github-bot: it never reads the account's login from GitHub. The webhook secret is the caller's own choice, typed into the webhook's form.
why.notes: postMessage creates a comment per post.
